Common.name: Scale-rayed wrasse
Description: Males build dish shaped nests and guard the eggs

Common.name: Hooknose
Description: Feeds on bottom crustaceans and polychaetes. spend most of their lives partly buried in sand, mud and gravel

Common.name: Starry ray
Description: Feed mainly on fish, crustaceans and polychaete worms, but also on hydroids, molluscs, cephalopods and echinoderms; known to be a scavenger.

Common.name: Launce
Description: During low light intensity (night and winter) they bury in the bottom

Common.name: Lesser sandeel
Description: Alternate between lying buried in the sandy substrate and swimming in schools in the water mass. They hibernate in winter buried in sand at depths of 20-50 cm

Common.name: Northern wolffish
Description: Feeds on sea gooseberries, medusas, small fishes, also echinoderms, crustaceans and mollusks (not so hard-shelled) (FishBase), benthic invertebrates with soft skeleton: sea urchins and brittle stars (Nedreaas, 2020)

Common.name: Atlantic wolffish
Description: Feeds on fishes, hard-shelled mollusks, crabs, lobsters, sea urchins and other echinoderms (FishBase); also mussels, whelks, and scallops (Wheeler, 1978)

Common.name: Spotted wolffish
Description: Feeds mainly on echinoderms, but also crustaceans, mollusks, fishes and worms

Common.name: European eel
Description: burrow in sediment

Common.name: Lesser silver smelt
Description: Feeds on bottom-living polychaetes, mollusks and crustaceans, also on pelagic invertebrates and fishes.

Common.name: Imperial scaldfish
Description: Found on sand, mud, shell and corals

Common.name: Scaldfish
Description: Live on mixed or muddy bottoms. Feed on small fishes and invertebrates

Common.name: Thor's scaldfish
Description: Found on the upper 100 m of the continental shelf. Feeds on small fishes and invertebrates

Common.name: Atlantic hookear sculpin
Description: Feed on polychaetes, small mollusks and very rarely small crustaceans

Common.name: Grey triggerfish
Description: Feeds on benthic invertebrates like mollusks and crustaceans. Adults guard the embryos nested in sand which hatched in about two days.

Common.name: Spinytail skate
Description: Benthic (Ref. 58426). Feed on all kinds of bottom animals

Common.name: Butterfly blenny
Description: Mainly nocturnal, they feed on small invertebrates.

Common.name: Tusk
Description: Feeds on crustaceans and shellfishes, benthic fishes (flatfishes and gurnard) and even on starfishes.

Common.name: Solenette
Description: Feeds on a wide range of bottom-living organisms, mainly crustaceans (copepods, amphipods, cumaceans), bivalve mollusks, and polychaetes.

Common.name: Dragonet
Description: Feeds on small invertebrates, mainly worms and crustaceans.

Common.name: Spotted dragonet
Description: Feeds on small bottom invertebrates mainly worms, snails and crustaceans.

Common.name: Reticulated dragonet
Description: Rests on the seabed

Common.name: Boarfish
Description: Feed on crustaceans or worms, mollusks

Common.name: Sea tadpole
Description: Feeds on benthic and pelagic crustaceans

Common.name: Rock cook
Description: Eggs are laid in the summer in a seaweed nest; Males build dish shaped nests and guard the eggs

Common.name: Red bandfish
Description: Lives in vertical burrows, terminating in an expanded chamber

Common.name: Red gurnard
Description: Feeds on benthic crustaceans, other invertebrates and bottom-dwelling fishes

Common.name: Streaked gurnard
Description: Feeds on crustaceans

Common.name: Tub gurnard
Description: Feeds on fish, crustaceans and mollusks. Has three isolated rays on the pectoral fin which function as legs on which the fish rests and also help in locating food on the soft bottom

Common.name: Longfin gurnard
Description: Food items include benthic crustaceans, worms, molluscs

Common.name: Thicklip grey mullet
Description: Adults feed mainly on benthic diatoms, epiphytic algae, small invertebrates and detritus

Common.name: Rabbit fish
Description: Feeds mainly on bottom-living invertebrates.

Common.name: Yarrell's blenny
Description: Feeds on bottom invertebrates (small mollusks, polychaetes, hydroids, sponges), also algae

Common.name: Shortnose greeneye
Description: Found on the continental shelf and upper slope over mud and clay bottom. Feeds mainly on bottom-living invertebrates.

Common.name: Five-bearded rockling
Description: Feed mainly on crustaceans, sometimes also on algae, polychaetes, gastropods and occasionally, small fish.

Common.name: Northern rockling
Description: Feed mostly on decapod crustaceans, lobsters, crabs, mysids and polychaetes

Common.name: Hollowsnout grenadier
Description: Feeds on a variety of benthic organisms, such as polychaetes, gastropods, cephalopods, numerous crustacean groups (copepods, gammarians, isopods, cumaceans, Natantia) and fish

Common.name: Spearsnouted grenadier
Description: Feeds primarily on small fish and bottom-living crustaceans.

Common.name: Rainbow wrasse
Description: Buries itself in sand at night or when frightened. Feeds on small gastropods, sea urchins, shrimps, worms, isopods and amphipods

Common.name: Polar sculpin
Description: Feeds on polychaetes, mysids, amphipods and pycnogonids

Common.name: Goldsinny wrasse
Description: Feed on bryozoans, crustaceans and gastropods

Common.name: Lumpfish
Description: Adults feed on ctenophores, medusas, small crustaceans, polychaetes, jelly fish and small fishes

Common.name: Common stingray
Description: Found over sandy and muddy bottoms, sometimes near rocky reefs. Feeds on bottom fishes, crustaceans and mollusks.

Common.name: Common dentex
Description: Feed on fish, mollusks and cephalopods

Common.name: Morocco dentex
Description: Feed mainly on crustaceans and fish but also takes mollusks

Common.name: European seabass
Description: Feed chiefly on shrimps and mollusks, also on fishes; Juveniles feed on invertebrates, taking increasingly more fish with age. Adults piscivorous

Common.name: Two-spotted clingfish
Description: Feeds mainly on benthic organisms

Common.name: Common skate
Description: Feeds on all kinds of bottom invertebrates and fish, including other skates

Common.name: Norwegian skate
Description: Feed on all kinds of bottom animals, mainly invertebrates and small fishes

Common.name: Longnosed skate
Description: Feeds on all kinds of bottom animals, mainly cephalopods and crustaceans

Common.name: Lesser weever
Description: Rest on the bottom, often buried with eyes and tip of first dorsal fin exposed

Common.name: Pearlfish
Description: Free-living, fairly deep. Assumed to feed on small invertebrates and fish

Common.name: Four-bearded rockling
Description: It feeds mainly on crustaceans, and to a lesser extent on worms and molluscs (Wheeler, 1978). Feed on flatfishes, amphipods, decapods, copepods, mysids, shrimps, isopods and other small crustaceans (FishBase).

Common.name: Snake pipefish
Description: Feed on small crustaceans and fish fry

Common.name: Grey gurnard
Description: Feeds on crustaceans, mostly shrimps and shore crabs; fishes, mostly gobies, flatfish, young herring and sand eels.

Common.name: Silvery pout
Description: Occurs in large schools over mud, muddy sand, gravel and rock bottoms. Feeds on small crustaceans and maybe worms.

Common.name: Atlantic cod
Description: Feed on wide range of crustaceans, worms, brittlestars and fishes especially

Common.name: Arctic rockling
Description: Feeds on decapod, amphipod, and euphausiid crustaceans, sometimes fishes are included in the diet

Common.name: Bigeye rockling
Description: Feed on crustaceans

Common.name: Shore rockling
Description: Feeds on fish, crustaceans, worms and algae(FishBase); feeds on crustaceans, small worms, and occasionaly fishes

Common.name: Three-bearded rockling
Description: Feed on shrimps, crabs, isopods, small fish, mollusks and polychaetes

Common.name: Tope shark
Description: Feeds on fishes (bottom as well as pelagic species), crustaceans, cephalopods, worms, and echinoderms

Common.name: Blackmouth catshark
Description: Feeds mainly on bottom invertebrates, including shrimps and cephalopods, but also on small pelagic bony fishes (lanternfishes) and other small elasmobranchs

Common.name: Three-spined stickleback
Description: "Following construction of a pit in a sandy substratum, the male lays down a mat of filamentous algae and other vegetation, may cover this partly with substratum carried to the nest by mouth, and finally forms a tunnel through which the female can pass during spawning"

Common.name: Witch
Description: Feeds on crustaceans, polychaetes, brittle stars and fishes

Common.name: Giant goby
Description: Macrobenthos feeder on hard substrates, feeds on green algae (Enteromorpha), crustaceans (amphipods, crabs), polychaetes, and insects

Common.name: Black goby
Description: Feed on crustaceans (larger amphipods, isopods, shrimps, mysids, small crabs), bivalves, gastropods, polychaetes, chironomid larvae, sometimes small fish

Common.name: Rock goby
Description: Macrobenthos feeder on hard substrates, they feed on crustaceans (larger amphipods, isopods, small crabs) and polychaetes; juveniles eat harpacticoid copepods, amphipods, polychaetes and mites

Common.name: Smooth sandeel
Description: has ability to burrow (Corbin, 1950)

Common.name: Bluemouth redfish
Description: They feed on both benthic and pelagic organisms (crustaceans, fishes, cephalopods, and echinoderms)

Common.name: Short snouted seahorse
Description: Feeds on small prey and organic debris (food items include: benthic crustaceans and worms

Common.name: Long rough dab
Description: Live on soft bottoms. Feed on invertebrates and small fishes (Fishbase); its food consists of crustaceans of various kinds, worms, molluscs, and brittlestars, and rather few fish (Wheeler)

Common.name: Halibut
Description: Feed mainly on other fishes (cod, haddock, pogge, sand-eels, herring, capelin), but also takes cephalopods, large crustaceans and other bottom-living animals.

Common.name: Corbin's sandeel
Description: For their winter hibernation (and when not feeding) sandeel bury themselves down to depths of twenty to thirty centimetres into the sand and sediment of the seabed (British seafishing website)

Common.name: Greater sandeel
Description: For their winter hibernation (and when not feeding) sandeel bury themselves down to depths of twenty to thirty centimetres into the sand and sediment of the seabed (British seafishing website)

Common.name: Twohorn sculpin
Description: Feeds on benthic polychaetes, crustaceans (Hyppolyte, Boreophausia), and large hyperiids (Phascolosoma)

Common.name: Ballan wrasse
Description: Eggs are laid in nest built from algae; Feed on crustaceans and mollusks

Common.name: Cuckoo wrasse
Description: Feed mainly on crustaceans but also fishes and mollusks and worms; Males build dish shaped nests and guard the eggs

Common.name: Diminutive goby
Description: Feeds on small crustaceans (decapods, amphipods), polychaetes and bivalves

Common.name: Four-spotted megrim
Description: Flatfish, inhabits soft bottoms.

Common.name: Megrim
Description: Flatfish, inhabits soft bottoms.

Common.name: Spiny gurnard
Description: Feeds on crustaceans, mainly amphipods

Common.name: Atlantic poacher
Description: Inhabits muddy bottoms. Feeds on pelagic and benthic crustaceans and polychaetes

Common.name: Spotted snake blenny
Description: Food consists of polychaetes and crustaceans

Common.name: Friess goby
Description: Cryptobenthic, burrowing in muddy sand or mud; often associated with a decapod crustacean Nephrops norvegicus; Feed on polychaetes, small crustaceans and mollusks. Eggs are deposited in burrows

Common.name: Sandy ray
Description: Feed on all kinds of bottom animals

Common.name: Shagreen ray
Description: Feed on all kinds of bottom animals, probably preferring fish

Common.name: Cuckoo ray
Description: Feed on all kinds of bottom animals

Common.name: Common dab
Description: Adults live mainly on sandy bottoms, from a few meters to about 100 m. Feed mainly on crustaceans and small fishes. (FishBase); eats almost any bottom-living invertebrate abundant locally which is small enough to be captured. Numerous kinds of small crustaceans, polychaete worms, and molluscs make up its bulk (Wheeler)

Common.name: Gelatinous snailfish
Description: Inhabits mud bottoms. Feeds on benthic and pelagic crustaceans and worms

Common.name: Striped seasnail
Description: Feeds primarily on crustaceans, occasionally fishes and polychaetes

Common.name: Montagus seasnail
Description: Feeds primarily on crustaceans; gammarid amphipods in intertidal; shrimps and small crabs in subtidal areas.

Common.name: Shanny
Description: Feeds on small benthic invertebrates, especially gastropods, barnacles and amphipods, and algae. Also, diet of crabs, polychaetes, isopods, copepods, limpets, mussels and small molluscs

Common.name: Blackbellied angler
Description: Rests on the seabed

Common.name: Angler
Description: It lies half-buried in the sediment waiting for its prey.

Common.name: Snake blenny
Description: living in Y-shaped tubes in the mud in 50-200 m depth. The burrows are believed to be used for parental care of the eggs. Feeds on small crustaceans, mollusks, brittle stars and worms

Common.name: Sars eelpout
Description: Found in muddy bottoms. Feeds on polychaetes, crustaceans and bivalves

Common.name: Greater eelpout
Description: Inhabits soft bottom areas; Feeds almost exclusively on ophiuroids (brittle stars)

Common.name: Gracile eelpout
Description: Food items include bivales, brittel stars, and worms

Common.name: Eelpout sp.
Description: Inhabits muddy bottoms with temperatures below 0°C. Feeds on small crustaceans like Themisto, Podocerus and Hemilamprops

Common.name: Snipefish
Description: adults normally live close to the bottom (normally in 50-350 m depth, adults feed on bottom invertebrates

Common.name: Roughhead grenadier
Description: Amphipods predominate in the diet, although polychaetes and various natant crustaceans are also important. Also feed on bivalves, isopods, echinoderms (notably ophiuroids), and ctenophores

Common.name: Haddock
Description: Feed mainly on small bottom-living organisms including crustaceans, mollusks, echinoderms, worms and fishes

Common.name: Whiting
Description: Feed on shrimps, crabs, mollusks, small fish, polychaetes and cephalopods

Common.name: Norway bullhead
Description: Feeds on small crustaceans (amphipods, decapods) and fishes

Common.name: Thickback sole
Description: Feeds on a wide range of small bottom-living organisms, mainly crustaceans (amphipods, shrimps), also polychaete worms and bivalve mollusks

Common.name: Lemon sole
Description: Feeds on a variety of small invertebrates, but polychaetes seem to dominate. (FishBase); Rather specialised feeder on polychaete worms, but it also eats numerous crustaceans and molluscs (Wheeler)

Common.name: Blue ling
Description: Feed on crustaceans and fish (flatfishes, gobies, rocklings)

Common.name: Spanish ling
Description: very similar to M. diptreygia as far as morphology, ecology and habitatpreferences are concerned (Bayhan et al., 2019), so class as same mode

Common.name: Common ling
Description: Feeds on fish (cod, herring, flatfish), lobsters, cephalopods and starfishes

Common.name: Common mora
Description: Feeds on fishes, crustaceans, mollusks and other invertebrates

Common.name: Red mullet
Description: Feeds on small benthic crustaceans, worms and mollusks; uses sensory barbels to sift sediment and detect prey

Common.name: Striped red mullet
Description: Feed on benthic organisms such as shrimps and amphipods, polychaetes, mollusks, and benthic fishes

Common.name: Starry smoothhound
Description: Feeds primarily on crustaceans (crabs, hermit crabs, lobsters and slipper lobsters)

Common.name: Smoothhound
Description: Feeds mainly on crustaceans, but also cephalopods and bony fishes

Common.name: Common eagle ray
Description: Feeds on benthic crustaceans, mollusks and fish

Common.name: Fourhourn sculpin
Description: Spawning takes place in shallow waters, male digs a groove in the gravel where pairing and egg laying occur.

Common.name: Arctic sculpin
Description: Feeds on fishes, large crustaceans, occasionally polychaetes and amphipods

Common.name: Shorthorn sculpin
Description: Found on rocky bottoms among algae. Feeds on small benthic amphipods

Common.name: Atlantic Hagfish
Description: Found on muddy bottoms where they hide in the mud

Common.name: Worm pipefish
Description: Feed on small crustaceans and fish fry

Common.name: Straightnose pipefish
Description: Feed on small crustaceans and fish fry

Common.name: Common Atlantic grenadier
Description: Feeds on benthic as well as pelagic animals like mysids, amphipods, small shrimps, copepods, isopods, ostracods and polychaete worms

Common.name: Snake blenny
Description: It lives buried inthe sand or mud, and in exceptional cases reaches lengths of30 cm (Matallanas 1980 in Hernandez et al., 2005).

Common.name: Axillary seabream
Description: Omnivorous, but prefer worms, mollusks and small crustaceans

Common.name: Blackspot seabream
Description: Omnivorous, but feed mainly on crustaceans, mollusks, worms and small fish

Common.name: Common pandora
Description: Omnivorous, but feed mainly on benthic invertebrates and small fishes

Common.name: Red porgy
Description: Feeds on crustaceans, fishes, and mollusks (diet items include worms, benthic crustaceans, echinoderms)

Common.name: Tompot blenny
Description: Feeds mainly on small crustaceans but its diet has not been fully studied

Common.name: Sand sole
Description: Feeds on a wide range of small marine bivalves; mainly on crustaceans such as amphipods, mysids, shrimps, decapods, bivalves and polychaetes

Common.name: Butterfish (gunnel)
Description: Feeds on small crustaceans, polychaetes, mollusks and fish eggs

Common.name: Greater forkbeard
Description: Feed mainly on crustaceans and fishes

Common.name: Flounder
Description: Nocturnal and burrowing (FishBase); feeds on a range of bottom-living invertebrates, especially molluscs such as cockles, worms and crustaceans (brown shrimps particularly). (Wheeler)

Common.name: Plaice
Description: Feed mainly on thin-shelled molluscs and polychaetes (FishBase); eat a wide range of bottom-living animals, especially molluscs, including burrowing species which often have their breathing siphons nipped off). They also eat large numbers of crustaceans and worms, and less often brittlestars and sandeels (Wheeler)

Common.name: Pollack
Description: feeds mainly on fishes, especially sandeels and memebers of the herrring and cod families, and on large numbers of crustaceans. Young eat crustaceans. Lie on seabed to ambush fish shoal above

Common.name: Wreckfish
Description: Feed on large crustaceans, cephalopods and benthic fishes

Common.name: Common goby
Description: Its burrowing habit allows it to survive low water levels and to avoid predators

Common.name: Sand goby
Description: Been shown to burrow into sediment to avoid predators

Common.name: Painted goby
Description: Inhabits gravel and sand; young may occur in shore pools. Feeds on crustaceans (copepods and amphipods)

Common.name: Blonde ray
Description: Feed on all kinds of benthic animals

Common.name: Thornback ray
Description: Nocturnal species. Feeds on all kinds of bottom animals, preferably crustaceans and fishes

Common.name: Small-eyed ray
Description: Feed on fishes. Ambush predator

Common.name: Spotted ray
Description: Species buries itself to avoid predation and ambush potential prey. Feeds mainly on crustaceans  with prey size increasing as it grows, also preys on benthic worms, cephalopods and small fishes

Common.name: Undulate ray
Description: Found on sandy bottoms of shelf waters. Feed on all kinds of bottom animals

Common.name: Round ray
Description: Feed on all kinds of bottom animals with preference for invertebrates like copepods, amphipods and mysids

Common.name: Sailray
Description: Feed on all kinds of bottom animals, invertebrates and fishes

Common.name: Tadpole fish
Description: Feeds on sea stars, crustaceans, worms, mollusks and small fish

Common.name: White skate
Description: A bottom-predator of bony fishes, other elasmobranchs, fish offal, crabs, shrimps, mysids, octopi, and cuttlefish

Common.name: Turbot
Description: Adults live on sandy, rocky or mixed bottoms; rather common in brackish waters. Feed mainly on other bottom-living fishes (sand-eels, gobies, etc.), and also, to a lesser extent, on larger crustaceans and bivalves

Common.name: Brill
Description: Lives on sandy or mixed bottoms; feeds on bottom-living fishes and larger crustaceans.

Common.name: Black Scorpionfish
Description: Solitary and sedentary. Common among rocks and algae. Feeds on small fishes (gobies, blennies), crustaceans and other invertebrates

Common.name: Red scorpionfish
Description: Feeds on fishes, crustaceans and mollusks

Common.name: Lesser spotted dogfish/smallspotted catshark
Description: Feed on a variety of benthic invertebrates, including mollusks, crustaceans, small cephalopods, polychaete worms, and small bony fishes

Common.name: Nurse hound
Description: Feed on bottom-living invertebrates such as mollusks and crustaceans and on demersal fishes (e.g. sharks, S. canicula).

Common.name: Comber
Description: Adults feed on fishes, cephalopods and crustaceans

Common.name: Painted comber
Description: Feed on fishes and crustaceans

Common.name: Sole
Description: They burrow into sandy and muddy bottoms. Adults feed on worms, mollusks and small crustaceans at night.

Common.name: Gilthead seabream
Description: Mainly carnivorous, accessorily herbivorous. Feed on shellfish, including mussels and oysters

Common.name: Sea stickleback
Description: Males build a nest from algae and debris, using kidney excrete as glue

Common.name: Black seabream
Description: builds nests buy using its tail on rocky or sandy bottoms and female lays eggs in nest

Common.name: Piked dogfish
Description: Feeds on a diversity of prey, ranging from comb jellyfish, squid, mackarel and herring to a wide array of benthic fishes, shrimps, crabs and even sea cucumbers (mainly feeds on fish but also some benthic prey so probaby low freqeuncy)

Common.name: Angelshark
Description:
Uses its large pectoral fins to fan out a depression in the seabed, then partly covers itself with sediment in ambush, leaving its eyes protruding. Feeds mainly on flatfishes, skates,
crustaceans and molluscs. Main prey items: common dab, plaice (Pleuronectiformes) (Ellis et al., 1996)

Common.name: Baillon's wrasse
Description: Males build dish shaped nests and guard the eggs

Common.name: Corkwing wrasse
Description: Feed on mollusks, hydroids, bryozoans, worms and various crustaceans; Seaweed nest built by male among rocks or in crevices

Common.name: Five-spotted wrasse
Description: Nest of seaweed built by male. Feed on mollusks, bivalves, gastropods, shrimps, sea-urchins and hydroids

Common.name: Greater pipefish
Description: Feeds mainly on small crustaceans, also molluscs

Common.name: Broadnosed pipefish
Description: Feeds on some benthic crustaceans

Common.name: Longspined bullhead
Description: Feeds on mysids, amphipods (gammarids), decapods, polychaetes, mollusks, ophiuroids and fishes

Common.name: Electric ray
Description: Feeds mainly on pelagic and benthic bony fishes and small sharks. often seen resting on or half-buried in the substrate during the day, becoming more active at night.

Common.name: Leopard-spotted goby
Description: Feed on crustaceans (copepods, amphipods, decapods), polychaetes, gastropods, algae

Common.name: Marbled electric ray
Description: Nocturnal, usually burying itself during the day with only the eyes and spiracle jutting out. Feeds on small benthic fishes (Trachurus, Mugil, Mullus, Dicentrarchus, Spondyliosoma, Boops, Labrus, Dascyllus, Pomacentrus) and crustaceans.

Common.name: Pompano
Description: Adults feed on small crustaceans, mollusks and fishes

Common.name: Greater weever
Description: Rest on the bottom, often buried with eyes and tip of first dorsal fin exposed

Common.name: Piper gurnard
Description: Feeds on shrimps and crabs

Common.name: Moustache sculpin
Description: Feeds on polychaetes and crustaceans

Common.name: Ripped sculpin
Description: Found on mud bottoms with some rocks.  Feeds on small crustaceans, usually amphipods and mysids, rarely polychaetes and fishes

Common.name: Bib
Description: Feeds on benthic crustaceans but also on small fish, mollusks and polychaetes

Common.name: Poor cod
Description: Feeds on crustaceans, small fish, and polychaetes

Common.name: Canary drum
Description: Feed on small shrimps, worms and other bottom invertebrates

Common.name: Shi drum
Description: Feed on bottom invertebrates.

Common.name: Norwegian topknot
Description: small flatfish occuring on rocky bottoms; feeds on worms, crustaceans, and young fishes

Common.name: Topknot
Description: Lives on stony or rocky ground in the algal zone, and feeds on small fishes and crustaceans

Common.name: Eckstroems topknot
Description: Occurs over rocky bottoms, less frequently on sandy bottoms. Feeds on small fish and invertebrates.

Common.name: John dory
Description: Feeds mainly on schooling bony fishes, occasionally on cephalopods and crustaceans

Common.name: Eelpout
Description: Feeds on gastropods, chironomids, crustaceans, eggs and fry of fishes
